cues.text: You left the washing on the highest roof in the city. The forecast has some thoughts about that.
The building was designed to carry water. Your shirts were not.
Seven floors of parking, and not one person thought to put a washing machine down here.
Someone stopped building halfway up. You, unfortunately, still have an errand.
A staircase this grand ought to lead to something important. Today it leads to socks.
The rain has no sense of urgency. That is because it is already where it needs to be.
Nearly there. Do not celebrate yet. Bringing the washing down is the other half of bringing it in.
There they are, enjoying the view at your expense. Take them off the line.
Laundry secured. Now get it back to the shelter. The weather is still keeping score.
Going down looks simpler from the top. So does most bad advice. Use the walls to slow your fall.
The shelter is below you. For once, the finish line is a perfectly ordinary patch of roof.
They are getting properly wet now. This is the part where a shortcut starts to look like a sensible idea.
Gravity offers an excellent delivery service. It does not handle complaints.
Home, and dry enough. Next time, perhaps use the balcony. It has considerably less city attached to it.
Too late. The rain has done the washing again. Give it another try; this time, bring the weather less sightseeing.
That was down. A bold interpretation of up.
The washing asked for a tumble dryer. You appear to have volunteered.
Excellent. Now you know that particular piece of floor from both sides.
A smaller correction next time. The entire building was a little excessive.
Same city. Lower address. The rent is probably better.
Do take your time. The rain has cleared its schedule.
Second level. You have climbed one whole storey of regret. Only the rest of the city remains.
Another floor above the boilers. The shirts are still upstairs; the excuses are multiplying.
The upper parking deck. You could leave your confidence here. Nobody is charging.
Another construction floor. Try to finish your jump more decisively than they finished this building.
The upper Ministry. All this authority, and nobody authorised a lift to the washing.
The second relay gallery. Plenty of aerials. Absolutely no drying signal.
The upper Crown. You can almost smell the damp cotton. That is motivation, apparently.
A service alley. Whoever left these barriers clearly expected a less ambitious pedestrian.
The first ramp is behind you. An excellent place to discover whether you packed patience.
You are above the street now. The washing has a better view and considerably worse judgement.
Those painted numbers were for maintenance crews. Today they measure the distance to your socks.
Old pipes ahead. They once moved heat through the city. You will have to supply your own momentum.
The loading shutters never opened again. At least they left room for a person with low expectations.
The upper heat gallery. Even the machinery has stopped working. You do not have that luxury.
Nothing here is switched on. Except the rain, which seems particularly committed.
Parking circulation. Built for cars, currently occupied by one person who forgot the laundry.
Mind the inspection beds. A raised floor is still a floor; it is just feeling important.
Another empty deck. Hundreds of spaces, and somehow you chose the roof for storage.
The broken joint is not a shortcut. The jump over it might be. There is a distinction.
Exposed shuttering. The workers left, but their timing problems stayed behind.
A crane, a beam, a very small margin. Your shirts had better appreciate this.
The upper construction gallery. The narrow steel is structural. Your confidence is optional.
There are lower maintenance roofs beneath you. Try to meet them only when necessary.
Welcome to the administrative passages. They made the walls enormous to keep the answers small.
These doors once led to offices. None of them leads to a conveniently placed tumble dryer.
The upper courtyards. A fine place to contemplate the decision that brought you here.
Follow the old service paint if you get turned around. It has been lost here longer than you.
Relay infrastructure. Everything points upward, which is encouraging until you look down.
The transfer girder is narrow because steel costs money. Courage was apparently free.
Another aerial gallery. Keep the movement small. The consequences have plenty of room.
The city is below your shoes now. A poor moment to start admiring the scenery while running.
The Crown approach. The wind has found the shirts before you have.
Those concrete blades frame the summit. They do not make the last jumps on your behalf.
Nearly the drying yard. The clothes are wet, but so far your plan is only questionable.
One final gallery. Once you collect the washing, every metre you climbed becomes a delivery address.
